Eskom versus Municipalities

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Small Town municipalities are collapsing, and Eskom is attaching their assets and bank accounts, but Eskom's hard line is hastening their demise even further

Unique Selling Point:
This is a perfect Carte Blanche where we have two very strong case study municipalities at war with Eskom that highlight the bigger picture of small town municipalities that have been hollowed out by corruption and are collapsing and the solution by Eskom to attach bank accounts and assets only hastens their demise further as Government looks the other way and ignores this elephant in the room. We will speak to those at the coal face in Map and Welkom

Summary:
In Maluti A Phofong, salaries arent paid, graves arent dug and water pipes arent replaced. In fact residents have formed committees and are doing the work of the municipality and paying for it out of their own pockets. In July Eskom attached the bank account over a R5.3 billion rand debt but now a Free State lawyer Bertus Maritz has taken on Eskom on behalf of MAP and Matjhabeng. He challenges Eskom's approach and says that this cannot be a solution as it will collapse Local government across the country and lead to lawlessness and chaos. Eskom is digging in its heels. This week a judgement is expected to decide what happens next, but he is prepared to take the matter all the way to the Constitutional court if he has to.

Further information:
MATJHABENG
Last month Matjhabeng municipality ceded over 139 farms to Eskom as security for the Eskom debt of R3.4 billion But the municipality has launched a counterclaim in court against Eskom of R4.5 billion for services rendered. Bertus argues that there are 36 wards in Matjhabeng and Eskom bills 26 of those wards directly. They take their money and walk away. He says that according to the constitution only local government can provide electricity in these areas and therefore Eskom owes the municipalities a surcharge on these 26 wards and he disputes the billions that Eskom says Matjhabeng is owed. As it is he says people simply cannot afford to pay as 50- 60% of people in the townships are unemployed so where is the money coming from? So Matjhabeng launched the counter claim against Eskom. The only way for the Municipality to get the money is to summons 50 000 people monthly. That is simply not practical and anyway they dont have the money. He says the model we have at the moment is simply not sustainable and Eskom action will lead to the collapse of local government in small towns. He says we cant keep saying we need to get money from National government because there isn’t any so his solution is to either ring fence 2% of vat to sort out these problems or look at losing layers of Provincial government that eat up huge amounts of money and provide very little value. He also questions why Eskom is not switching off Soweto, its biggest creditor that owes R17 billion of the R31 billion owed to Eskom. He also says SALGA and the Municipalities are considering a class action against Eskom

Script:


THE PERFECT STORM: ESKOM VERSUS FS MUNICS FINAL SCRIPT TX SUNDAY 22nd NOVEMBER 2020 FACT CHECKED

Commentary On
The day after lockdown Tseko Mothamaha started his new job as Municipal manager of Maluti A Phofung, a municipality that includes Phutadijaba and Harrismith in the Free State.

Tseko
There is huge potential in this municipality, it could be one of the metro’s

Commentary Two
But Mothamaha has a mountain to climb, because this municipality has been hollowed out by its former leadership, and even when it was placed under administration it didn’t recover

Up sound Festival

For nearly five years this was the place of Dipontsho or festivals, led by the former Mayor Vusi Tshabalala.

Up sound Festival

An ally of Ace Magashule, Tshabalala strutted his stuff in fancy suits and expensive cars, and is alleged to have redirected legitimate pre-paid electricity payments to his own network.

Angry crowd protesting

Eventually angry residents and councilors got rid of him, but by then the municipality owed Eskom R2.7 billion rand. That was in 2018, and when we put the allegations to him, he told us that he doesn’t answer allegations.

Derek Watts 2018 story
But I think its proper that you do reply to allegations

Commentary Three
Vusi Tshabalala then drove off into the sunset, promoted by the ANC to chief whip in the Free State legislature.

But in his wake, he left an Eskom debt that has now ballooned to R5.5 billion, which threatens the entire municipality of around 900 thousand people, unless Tseko Mothamaha can find a solution. To make matters worse, residents don’t want to pay for electricity

Tseko
There is huge illegal connections and tampering in this municipality. Its more than 90%



Commentary Four
He sent in teams to cut the illegal connections, started fixing the towns, and increasing payment levels, but Eskom was impatient.

Tseko
We pleaded with Eskom that we need to be given a chance, about 3 months or so. How are we going to pay the current account and the debt we inherited of R5.5 billion? But Eskom guys in Bloem were reluctant.

LINK
Eskom is on a ruthless drive to get paid by defaulting municipalities and in the Free State the courts have become the battleground

Commentary five
Free State municipalities, including Maluti- A- Phofung owe Eskom R13 billion rand. Agnes Mlambo is General manager for KZN and Free State, and tasked to recover the money

Agnes
I have personally engaged Maluti. And we've written to Maluti, we've made a couple of offers, they had expiry dates, those dates came and gone. And they had not responded to any of our letters.

Commentary Six
But Mothamaha disagrees, and was shocked by what Eskom did next. In July, just a day after treasury dished out the equitable share of R234 million for basic services, Eskom attached their bank account

Tseko
You can imagine as an accounting officer trying to bring confidence, the next thing, the account is attached

Commentary Seven
The impact was devastating. So Maluti -A-Phofung went to court to get the attachment lifted. Bertus Maritz is the attorney representing them.

Mac
Eskom can argue you owe them R5.5 billion?
Bertus
Yes but then why wait ten years before you act and then all of a sudden you try and collect everything at once, knowing it’s one of the poorest areas, you cannot operate like that and say it’s in good faith

Commentary Eight
MAP ran out of money for almost everything- including chemicals to purify the town’s water


Tseko
We don’t have money anymore we have small chemicals so we are just hoping we can win the case

Commentary nine
The Firemen, the grave diggers -all were reluctant to work without payment

Tseko
We are talking to guys to help us dig and with the mercy of God they are helping us

Commentary ten
Later Eskom released around R90 million for salaries and running costs, but by early November, those funds had been drained.

Up sound protest

Staff pensions and medical aids weren’t paid, so they didn’t go work, and some protested outside the offices

Mac
They didn't even have money to buy chemicals to purify water, how do you balance it when the human impact is quite huge?
Agnes
So the reason why the bank account remained attached was not because we did not want to get into the table and negotiate. It's because they opted to go to the courts
Mac
So Ms Mlambo when you put all of these options for MAP perform, what is their response?
Agnes
There was never any response. And the other thing that you also need to note is that we charge Maluti or the municipalities about R1 09 cents per kilowatt hour. They in turn to charge their own customers, at Maluti specifically R2 27. Now that's more than double mark-up that they make. Now, the question is what happens to the monies that they receive from the customers, if they're not paying Eskom?

Commentary eleven
And Maluti argues they make money off electricity, AND they are obliged by law to deliver services, while Eskom is accelerating their diminishing revenue base.

Bertus
In MAP they are going backwards at a rate of approximately R45 million a month. They deliver water, sewerage and refuse, you cannot stop it its constitutional rights.



Commentary twelve
In September Eskom sent another writ, ordering Maluti to pay R2.4 billion plus R725 million rand in interest- a total of R3.1 billion rand.

Bertus
Then we went back to court to say now it becomes really silly. Just on the collection rate of MAP monthly is between R15 and R20 million. If you take that and divide it into the R3.5 billion it will take 17 years, alternatively for the next four years if you take all the income of MAP and the equitable share then you will then be able to pay that debt, how will the municipality survive in four years.

Commentary Thirteen
As November began, Maluti A Phofung had staggered through 2020 with no bank account for almost half the year. Residents dropped their rubbish outside the municipal offices. The MM was desperate.

Tseko
Service delivery has collapsed here because of Eskom

Commentary fourteen
On the 9th of November Map’s legal team waited anxiously for the judgement- delivered remotely.

LINK
They’ve been waiting for months to see if the court will allow them access back into their bank accounts. It’s now judgement time.

JUDGE Corne Van Zyl
The third respondent is ordered to release the hold on the first applicants funds

Commentary fifteen
Eskom lost, and was ordered to pay Maluti’s costs. But Map’s victory may be short lived.

Agnes
We are appealing it and we are reviewing the judgement.
Mac
Do you feel that this is the only option that you have?
Agnes
I'm really open for any option for us to get the money. The intention for us is not to frustrate Maluti the municipality. We continue to provide electricity to the municipalities. We are not getting paid for what we provide, and yet we need to also make sure that our suppliers are being paid.



Commentary Sixteen
Three hours to the west of Maluti lies Matjhabeng – another defaulting Free State municipality represented by Bertus Maritz.

MAC
It seems like its crunch time for them if Eskom doesn’t get this money the whole country fails so where do you even begin?
Bertus
If we do not fix the current issues that we are raising, local government will collapse and in fact its already collapsing

Commentary Seventeen
Welkom, Matjhabeng’s once pristine mining town is decaying. They owe Eskom R3.5 billion

Agnes
Well Matjhabeng pays randomly, the last two months, they have not paid us

Commentary Eighteen
Rubbish is dumped randomly, pylons are rusting and falling over, broken pipes aren’t repaired, and worst of all, the place is drowning in sewerage. Resident and business owner Chris Nel

CHRIS
Not one of the sewerage plants is working. Nothing. So the raw sewerage is just running through it or being pumped directly into the river system. One of them is submerged in a dam-you can't get to it except by boat.

Commentary seventeen
He took us to Klip Pan, a plant we filmed in 2008 when the pumps broke- now its underwater as the municipality failed to fix the pumps, and they pump raw sewerage straight into what has become a dam-and the only evidence of the treatment works is this rooftop sticking out above the water.

Near the Thabong township is another abandoned and broken treatment works

Chris
And we can see a dramatic decrease in our clientele that's just leaving Welkom. They just saying we had enough and they go out, people actually moving back to Joburg. Can you believe that?

Commentary Eighteen
Eskom attached Matjhabeng’s bank account too, but to keep Eskom at bay they offered Eskom 139 farms worth R2.5 billion as collateral



LINK
Matjhabeng didn’t take too kindly to the attachment of their bank account, so they took a more aggressive legal approach and launched a counterclaim against Eskom to say the utility owes them money.

Commentary nineteen
Maritz argues that Eskom is muscling in on local government jurisdiction by providing electricity directly in 26 wards and depriving the municipality of funds for services

BERTUS
If I can break down Matjhabeng expenditure in a month for you. R65 million for Eskom, R65 million for Sedibeng water,R60 million for salaries, R50 million for running costs and then because of financial troubles there is about R50 million by judgements, now if you add up all these amounts it’s about R230 million
MAC
Which is about the budget of the municipality every month?
Bertus
We are only billing R183 million a month!

LINK CONCOURT
So what happens next? Will this battle go all the way to the Constitutional court because Eskom or the municipalities cannot find a way out of this stalemate?

Commentary Twenty
The municipalities argue that Eskom is running to court instead of using the intergovernmental channels to sort out their differences, Eskom says they have tried that, and the municipalities ignore those decisions

Mac
What do you think would resolve this issue?
AGNES
For us as Eskom if the electricity business is a burden to them, we are more than willing to take it over. That way we do not have to talk about a debt that is accumulating simply because they are not paying over.

Bertus
Either agree around the table or go to the CON COURT and get one ruling once and for all that will clear up the mess

Commentary twenty one
Maritz argues this is now a national problem. In the meantime no one is winning, not Eskom, not the municipalities and certainly not South Africans who depend on both of them.

THE END





PROMO ONE
Eskom’s debt is South Africa’s Achilles heel. To get its money back its taken a hardline with defaulting municipalities who are on the brink of collapse

PROMO TWO
Eskom is impatient for the nine billion rand owed to it by two Free State Municipalities, but when the courts froze the bank account of Maluti- A-Phofung, the impact was devastating

PROMO THREE
After years of corruption and maladministration Eskom is trying to recover debt from municipalities that are themselves close to collapse. Now the battles have gone to court



NAMES

TSEKO MOTHAMAHA
MUNICIPAL MANAGER: MALUTI-A-PHOFUNG

AGNES MLAMBO
GENERAL MANAGER: ESKOM DISTRIBUTION, KZN & FREE STATE

BERTUS MARITZ
ATTORNEY: BOKWA ATTORNEYS

CHRIS NEL: BUSINESSMAN, WELKOM

AGNES For us as Eskom if the electricity business is a burden to them, we are more than willing to take it over. That way we do not have to talk about a debt that is accumulating simply because they are not paying over. Bertus Either agree around the table or go to the CON COURT and get one ruling once and for all that will clear up the mess Commentary twenty one Maritz argues this is now a national problem. In the meantime no one is winning, not Eskom, not the municipalities and certainly not South Africans who depend on both of them. THE END PROMO ONE Eskom’s debt is South Africa’s Achilles heel. To get its money back its taken a hardline with defaulting municipalities who are on the brink of collapse PROMO TWO Eskom is impatient for the nine billion rand owed to it by two Free State Municipalities, but when the courts froze the bank account of Maluti- A-Phofung, the impact was devastating PROMO THREE After years of corruption and maladministration Eskom is trying to recover debt from municipalities that are themselves close to collapse. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Small Town municipalities are collapsing, and Eskom is attaching their assets and bank accounts, but Eskom's hard line is hastening their demise even further
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This is a perfect Carte Blanche where we have two very strong case study municipalities at war with Eskom that highlight the bigger picture of small town municipalities that have been hollowed out by corruption and are collapsing and the solution by Eskom to attach bank accounts and assets only hastens their demise further as Government looks the other way and ignores this elephant in the room. We will speak to those at the coal face in Map and Welkom
metadata.Summary: In Maluti A Phofong, salaries arent paid, graves arent dug and water pipes arent replaced. In fact residents have formed committees and are doing the work of the municipality and paying for it out of their own pockets. In July Eskom attached the bank account over a R5.3 billion rand debt but now a Free State lawyer Bertus Maritz has taken on Eskom on behalf of MAP and Matjhabeng. He challenges Eskom's approach and says that this cannot be a solution as it will collapse Local government across the country and lead to lawlessness and chaos. Eskom is digging in its heels. This week a judgement is expected to decide what happens next, but he is prepared to take the matter all the way to the Constitutional court if he has to.
metadata.Further information: MATJHABENG Last month Matjhabeng municipality ceded over 139 farms to Eskom as security for the Eskom debt of R3.4 billion But the municipality has launched a counterclaim in court against Eskom of R4.5 billion for services rendered. Bertus argues that there are 36 wards in Matjhabeng and Eskom bills 26 of those wards directly. They take their money and walk away. He says that according to the constitution only local government can provide electricity in these areas and therefore Eskom owes the municipalities a surcharge on these 26 wards and he disputes the billions that Eskom says Matjhabeng is owed. As it is he says people simply cannot afford to pay as 50- 60% of people in the townships are unemployed so where is the money coming from? So Matjhabeng launched the counter claim against Eskom. The only way for the Municipality to get the money is to summons 50 000 people monthly. That is simply not practical and anyway they dont have the money. He says the model we have at the moment is simply not sustainable and Eskom action will lead to the collapse of local government in small towns. He says we cant keep saying we need to get money from National government because there isn’t any so his solution is to either ring fence 2% of vat to sort out these problems or look at losing layers of Provincial government that eat up huge amounts of money and provide very little value. He also questions why Eskom is not switching off Soweto, its biggest creditor that owes R17 billion of the R31 billion owed to Eskom. He also says SALGA and the Municipalities are considering a class action against Eskom
